title: timebucket-merger-edgecase-produces-phantom-usage-for-transient-keys
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: After a sequence of late-arriving usage events and a shard handover, the timebucket merge path can produce persistent, spurious usage records for short-lived API keys. These "phantom" usage items inflate per-key and per-route counters, lead to unexpected metering, and may cause transient throttles for affected keys. This ticket tracks investigation, mitigation, and a durable fix for the timebucket merger/compaction codepath.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Instrument a test tenant with a large number of short-lived API keys (create/delete frequently).
2) Drive bursty traffic with artificially skewed timestamps: send a set of requests where ~5% have timestamps delayed by 30-90s (simulate clock skew / network delay).
3) Trigger a shard reassignment (move shard owner) or force a compaction cycle, so the timebucket merger executes on overlapping windows.

4) Observe per-key counters and per-route aggregates in staging billing logs and Grafana: some deleted keys show non-zero historic usage after compaction, and rate limit checks show unexpected credit consumption for subsequent requests.
5) Re-run with debug logging enabled for the merger path to capture event ordering and merge decisions.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: out-of-order events during merge (late-arriving deltas) are applied to a synthetic timebucket because the merger picks an earliest-seen timestamp as the canonical bucket instead of respecting shard watermarks.
Reproducer built in staging that simulates late-arriving deltas using kafka-proxy with timestamp override. Reproducer reliably triggers phantom usage in ~1/20 compactions with current heuristics.

Log snippets show merger applied a delta with timestamp T-70s to an already-compact bucket for key k that was previously soft-deleted; subsequent compaction preserved the combined total instead of dropping event due to tombstone semantics.
Rate-limit enforcement consults the compaction output; because phantom entries survive, enforcement sees extra tokens charged leading to transient client throttles and billing mismatches.
Edge conditions observed when: (a) key lifecycle is short (create -> traffic -> delete) and (b) ingest happens across two or more broker partitions with non-monotonic delivery ordering.
root_cause: Merger/compaction logic treats late-arriving deltas as authoritative for bucket assignment without verifying against shard-level monotonic watermark or tombstone markers. When a key has been deleted and the deletion tombstone hasn't propagated to the compaction worker, a late delta can be merged into a new persisted bucket, resulting in a persistent, incorrectly attributed usage record.
current_status: Reproducer confirmed in staging. Holding mitigations live lane: disable aggressive compaction for affected shards and enable strict watermark check in shadow path. Patch PR open for conservative merge gating.
immediate_mitigation: 1) Roll out a staging-only change to gate compaction: compaction will skip buckets containing keys with tombstone timestamps later than the candidate delta. 2) Short-term fix deployed to 3% of shards behind a feature flag to limit blast radius. 3) Customer-facing mitigation: disable billing-sensitive auto-rollups for customers who report anomalies (support-runbook).
long_term_solution: 1) Change compaction algorithm to consult per-shard monotonic watermark and ignore/queue deltas older than the watermark for reconciliation via the late-event processor.
2) Add deterministic merge idempotency: attach ingest-sequence-id per delta and use it to deduplicate during merge so late duplicates can't resurrect deleted keys.
3) Enhance tombstone propagation: make delete events carry a compactation-epoch marker so compaction workers can treat tombstones as highest precedence during merges.
4) Add unit + integration tests that simulate cross-partition out-of-order delivery and validate no persistent buckets are created for deleted keys.
5) Add a monitoring alert (grafana + alertmanager) to detect sudden appearance of non-zero usage for keys flagged in deletion logs within last 5m.
acceptance_criteria: Reproducer runs 100x in CI harness with late-arriving events and shows zero phantom usage after fixes are applied.
Staging rollout to 10% shards for 48h with no new phantom usage incidents and no measurable regression in compaction latency (>5% increase allowed).
Production rollout plan documented and rollback tested; feature flag for conservative-merge gating can be toggled without data corruption.
Consequence analysis completed: billing reconciliation script handles any prior phantom entries and credits affected customers as needed.
deployment_plan: Phase 1 (hotfix): deploy conservative merge gating to 3% shards behind feature flag; monitor for 24h.
Phase 2 (staged): deploy idempotent-merge PR to 10% shards; enable late-event queuing; validate in staging for 48h.
Phase 3 (prod): full roll to all shards with monitoring and throttled ramp; post-roll run of reconciliation job for prior phantom usage entries.
Rollback: flip feature flag to disable gating and/or revert merge PR; run verification suite to ensure no more phantom entries.

notes_for_support: If customers report unexpected throttles or billing spikes, run support playbook: check recent deletion events for keys in question, query compaction output for non-zero post-deletion usage, and escalate to engineering with reproduction trace id.
Temporary workaround: enable per-customer conservative compaction flag which prevents compaction from persisting buckets for keys deleted within last 5 minutes.
